BINDING_HPO_DECISION.consequence: Neither half alone discharges the decision. fail_closed_on_error.rule: If the provider status cannot be READ, the subject is REFUSED. If the provider call ERRORS, the subject is REFUSED. Neither is treated as verified, and neither is treated as a logout.
fail_closed_on_error.how_it_composes_with_what_exists: lib/auth/identity.ts already returns AUTH_UNAVAILABLE rather than a null session for a thrown createClient() at :95-101 or a thrown getUser() at :106-108, and lib/auth/database-context.ts:187-188 already maps AUTH_UNAVAILABLE to 503. Packet B ADDS NO NEW ERROR PATH: it requires that the existing AUTH_UNAVAILABLE path continue to refuse, and forbids any catch that converts it into a verified subject.
fail_closed_on_error.the_prohibited_shape: A try around the read whose catch assigns verified equals true, and every rewriting of it, including a default parameter of true, a nullish coalesce to true, and an if-we-could-not-determine-it-do-not-block-the-user comment. M-B-3 is the mutation control for exactly this shape.
fail_closed_on_error.why_a_503_and_not_a_redirect: An auth outage is not an unverified user. Redirecting an outage to the verification-pending page would tell every signed-in user that their email is unconfirmed, which is false, and would generate support load proportional to the outage. The existing 503 mapping is the honest answer and is preserved.

PROVIDER_TRUTH_SOURCE.cardinality_rule: EXACTLY ONE MODULE MAY DERIVE THE PREDICATE. The derivation from the provider field to the boolean lives in one place and is imported everywhere else. A second derivation is a second source of truth, and the two can disagree by one release. Sentinel S-IA-PREDICATE-CARDINALITY asserts this mechanically.

DUAL_GATE.status: BINDING. Both halves required. Neither discharges the other.

GATE_A_PROVIDER.requirement: The hosted authentication provider MUST require and perform email confirmation for email/password signup.
GATE_A_PROVIDER.concrete_setting: Supabase Auth, [auth.email] enable_confirmations true, on each hosted project, staging and production, plus a working sender for the confirmation mail.
GATE_A_PROVIDER.what_it_and_only_it_provides: The mail is actually SENT, the link actually WORKS, and email_confirmed_at is actually SET when the subject clicks it. No amount of application code can produce any of those three.
GATE_A_PROVIDER.what_it_does_NOT_provide: It does not gate any non-signup entry path, it does not survive a dashboard misconfiguration, and it leaves no evidence in the repository. An application that trusts it blindly has an unauditable control.
GATE_A_PROVIDER.evidence_obligation: A hosted observation, captured by the operator, recording enable_confirmations for each hosted project. THIS LANE PERFORMS NO ENVIRONMENT MUTATION AND MAKES NO SUCH OBSERVATION. See HOSTED_PROVIDER_STATE.

GATE_B_APPLICATION.requirement: Uellix application code MUST INDEPENDENTLY refuse protected customer entry when the authenticated subject email is not provider-confirmed.
GATE_B_APPLICATION.independence_meaning: The refusal must hold even if Gate A is off. That is testable offline with a mocked provider subject, which is why every negative control in the companion manifest is a pure unit control and none of them requires a live provider.
GATE_B_APPLICATION.what_it_and_only_it_provides: Coverage of every entry point in entry_point_closed_world, including the three, E3, E7 and E9, that no provider setting reaches, and a durable, reviewable, testable artifact in the repository.
GATE_B_APPLICATION.what_it_does_NOT_provide: It cannot prove the confirmation mail is deliverable. An application gate with Gate A off refuses every real user forever, because nothing ever sets email_confirmed_at. THAT IS AN OUTAGE, AND IT IS THE SPECIFIC RISK OF SHIPPING GATE B FIRST.
GATE_B_APPLICATION.sequencing_consequence: Gate A SHOULD be enabled on a given environment BEFORE or AT THE SAME TIME AS Gate B reaches it. This is an operational ordering, not a code dependency; it is recorded in OPEN_FINDINGS F-IA-2 rather than encoded in the application, because encoding it would mean the application deciding to fail open when it thinks the provider is off, which is M-B-3.

DUAL_GATE.the_asymmetry_that_makes_both_necessary: Gate A is the only thing that can make verification HAPPEN. Gate B is the only thing that can make verification MATTER. Neither substitutes for the other, and the failure modes are opposite: A-without-B is a control that is not enforced, B-without-A is an enforcement with nothing to satisfy it.

AUTH_MECHANISM_SEMANTICS.governing_rule: THE RULE CONSUMES PROVIDER-CONFIRMED IDENTITY STATE. IT NEVER CONSUMES THE AUTHENTICATION MECHANISM. One predicate, evaluated per request against email_confirmed_at, applies to every mechanism below. The subsections do not create per-mechanism rules; they record what the SINGLE rule yields for each mechanism, and where the routing, not the predicate, must differ.

the_flow_keying_prohibition.rule: No branch of the verification gate may be keyed on how the session was created: not on app_metadata.provider, not on a recovery marker, not on the presence of a next parameter, not on which action or route handler produced the session.
the_flow_keying_prohibition.why: Section 4 gives two failure directions and a flow-keyed rule produces BOTH. Keyed to refuse a flow, it falsely refuses provider-confirmed OAuth subjects. Keyed to trust a flow, it creates precisely the recovery bypass section 4 forbids. A single predicate over provider state has neither failure mode, and it needs no per-mechanism maintenance as mechanisms are added.
the_flow_keying_prohibition.structural_reason_this_is_not_merely_sty: app/auth/callback/route.ts:14 is ONE handler that serves email confirmation links, magic links, OAuth PKCE returns and recovery returns, all through the same exchangeCodeForSession call. THE APPLICATION CANNOT RELIABLY TELL THESE APART AT THAT LINE. A flow-keyed rule would have to guess the flow from a URL parameter, which is client-supplied. Provider state is the only thing available there that is not.

password_recovery.the_hazard_section_4_names: Recovery must not become an alternate path that bypasses verification policy. At BASE it plainly is one: a recovery return lands in the same smart-redirect as a login and reaches /app/onboarding or /app/dashboard with no verification question asked anywhere.
password_recovery.packet_b_rule_part_1_the_gate_is_not_byp: Because the gate is a per-request read of provider state and is NOT keyed on the flow, a recovery session is evaluated exactly like any other session. If email_confirmed_at is set the subject proceeds; if it is not, the subject is refused at the same four enforcement points. There is no recovery-shaped hole to close, because there is no recovery-shaped branch to begin with. THIS IS THE ARCHITECTURAL REASON THE FLOW-KEYING PROHIBITION IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY.
password_recovery.packet_b_rule_part_2_the_password_change: E12, app/(public)/reset-password/actions.ts, is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the enforcement points. Refusing an unverified subject the ability to set a password would trap an account that cannot recover and cannot be recovered, and a password change grants access to NOTHING: the subject who completes it is returned to /login at :33 and meets the gate on the next authenticated entry. The refusal belongs where access is granted, not where a credential is rotated.

packet_b_rule_part_3_the_provider_side_e.why_it_does_not_block: The application is correct under BOTH answers, precisely because it re-reads provider state per request rather than modelling the provider side effects. If GoTrue does promote, the subject becomes verified and is admitted, legitimately, having proven mailbox control. If it does not, the subject stays refused. The application asserts neither.
packet_b_rule_part_3_the_provider_side_e.what_is_forbidden: Any application code that ASSUMES either answer, for example marking a subject verified after a recovery, or specially refusing a session that arrived via recovery. Both are flow-keying. N-B-5 and M-B-4 are the controls.

invitation_acceptance.the_tension_stated_honestly: An invitation is evidence that SOMEBODY who controls an organisation believes this address should have access. It is NOT evidence that the person now holding the session controls that mailbox. A stolen or forwarded invitation link plus an unverified signup at the invited address produces a member of a tenant the subject never proved they own.

The invitation is not consumed, not expired and not revoked by the refusal: the subject is routed to the verification-pending destination and returns to the same link afterwards. The token-carrying URL must be preserved across the refusal so the journey completes without the inviter re-issuing anything.
invitation_acceptance.explicitly_not_absorbed: Packet B does not touch invitation issuance, expiry, revocation, the INVITATION_SENT audit ordering, or Resend delivery. See BOUNDARIES.

already_authenticated_legacy_accounts.the_case: Accounts created while Gate A was off have a null email_confirmed_at and hold valid sessions. Turning on Gate A does not retroactively confirm them; turning on Gate B refuses them.
already_authenticated_legacy_accounts.packet_b_rule: They are refused, correctly: their mailbox control was never proven. They are routed to the verification-pending destination, from which a confirmation mail can be requested. This is a MIGRATION consequence, not a defect, and it is the single largest operational impact of this packet. Recorded as OPEN_FINDINGS F-IA-5 so it is planned rather than discovered.

ROUTING_CONTRACT_PACKET_B.applies_to: An AUTHENTICATED subject. An UNAUTHENTICATED subject is entirely out of scope and every existing redirect to /login is preserved verbatim at every site, exactly as Packet A preserved it.
ROUTING_CONTRACT_PACKET_B.evaluation_order_is_normative: B0 is evaluated BEFORE every rule of Packet A ROUTING_CONTRACT wherever that contract is evaluated. An implementation that evaluates B0 after R1 or after R2 produces a different destination for the same principal, so the order is part of the contract.

B0_VERIFICATION_PRECEDES_TENANCY.rule: If the authenticated subject email is not provider-confirmed, the request is REFUSED and routed to the verification-pending destination. No tenancy question is asked. No enumeration is performed. No carrier is read, written or cleared. No organisation is created. No membership is created.
B0_VERIFICATION_PRECEDES_TENANCY.precondition: principal resolved AND emailVerified is false.
B0_VERIFICATION_PRECEDES_TENANCY.why_it_precedes_R1_super_admin: R1 is a DESTINATION rule: it decides WHERE a super-admin without a membership goes. B0 is an IDENTITY-PROOF rule: it decides WHETHER the subject has proven they own the address the account is keyed to. A privilege bit read from public.users.is_super_admin is not a proof of mailbox control, and an unverified super-admin is the single worst account-takeover shape in the system. Ordering B0 first is therefore fail-closed.
B0_VERIFICATION_PRECEDES_TENANCY.why_this_is_NOT_a_redesign_of_platform_a: Section 6 forbids using Packet B to redesign platform-admin identity, and this does not. SUPERADMIN_BOUNDARY is untouched: super-admins still reach tenant data through their own explicit door, they are still never routed to the tenant selector, R1 keeps its position ahead of every selector question and keeps its destination. B0 applies the SAME predicate to them as to everyone, which is the opposite of a special identity design. The operational escape is provider-side and needs no code: confirming the address at the provider clears B0.
B0_VERIFICATION_PRECEDES_TENANCY.counter_argument_recorded: A reviewer may hold that a platform operator locked out by their own unverified address is a worse outcome than an unverified operator session. That argument is real and is recorded rather than suppressed. It is REJECTED here because the lockout is recoverable by a provider action that requires no deploy, while the alternative is unrecoverable if exploited. If the independent audit adjudicates otherwise, the change is a REORDERING of B0 relative to R1 and nothing else: the predicate, the destination and the other three enforcement points are unaffected.

B2_MINIMUM_SAFE_DESTINATION.derivation_not_preference: The destination must satisfy four measured constraints simultaneously. One: it must be reachable by an AUTHENTICATED subject, so it cannot redirect authenticated users away. Two: it must NOT be behind any of the four enforcement points, or it redirects to itself, the exact failure app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx:8-30 records as MEASURED in production, ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, dozens of 307s, zero 500s. Since B1-P1 is requireAuth() itself, the destination cannot call requireAuth() and cannot sit under app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx, whose only statement is requireAuth() at :76. Three: it must be able to READ the principal, to show which address is awaiting confirmation and to offer a resend, which is possible without requireAuth, because resolving a principal and enforcing a gate are already separate concerns in this codebase, lib/auth/session.ts:101 getCurrentUser does not redirect. Four: it must not be swept up by the proxy isProtected predicate, which is exactly pathname.startsWith('/app') or pathname.startsWith('/admin') at lib/supabase/proxy.ts:80. Only a route outside app/(authenticated)/ and outside /app satisfies all four. app/(public)/ satisfies all four and app/(public)/layout.tsx makes no auth call of any kind: grep for requireAuth, getCurrentUser, loadRequestPrincipal and redirect over it returns zero hits.

MUST NOT silently fall through to organisation onboarding. /app/onboarding is NOT an acceptable destination for an unverified subject: it is the organisation CREATION form, which is the highest-value unverified write in the closed world.
MUST NOT expose protected product routes, including any partial render, any layout chrome that names an organisation, or any streamed shell before the redirect.

MUST NOT enumerate selectable memberships. Enumeration is a read of tenancy facts about a subject who has not proven mailbox control, and it happens BEFORE the routing decision in Packet A R2, which is precisely why B0 precedes R2.
MUST NOT emit an audit row. See BOUNDARIES.audit_verb_is_out_of_scope for the measured database reason.

PACKET_A_PRESERVATION.claim: For any subject with email_confirmed_at set, the observable behaviour of the application after Packet B is IDENTICAL to its behaviour at BASE.
PACKET_A_PRESERVATION.why_the_claim_is_structurally_credible: B0 is a PREFIX, not a rewrite. It returns control to Packet A R1 through R5 untouched when the predicate passes, and it never reads, writes or clears the carrier, never enumerates, and never changes a destination.
PACKET_A_PRESERVATION.how_it_is_PROVEN_rather_than_asserted: P-B-2 through P-B-6 re-drive the Packet A OWN control scenarios, zero candidates, exactly one candidate, two candidates, stale carrier, super-admin, and RETURN SITE 3, with a VERIFIED subject, and require the SAME destinations the Packet A manifest requires. If any of them changes, Packet B has silently redesigned tenancy and the node stops.
PACKET_A_PRESERVATION.the_specific_regression_this_guards: An implementer who places B0 AFTER Packet A R2, rather than before, would leave enumeration running for unverified subjects. That change is invisible in the verified path, every positive control still passes, and is caught only by the N-B-2 assertion that NO enumeration occurs on the unverified path. This is why N-B-2 asserts on the ENUMERATOR CALL and not merely on the destination.
